Dark glossy beads on pale rods -> remain broadly in place, with no obvious sliding toward the reckoning beam.

Changing angle from slow pan -> moves light and shadow across the rounded bead surfaces.
caption: The video captures a tight close-up of an aged wooden abacus, its dark glossy beads strung on pale tan rods with a couple of silver shafts among them. A reckoning beam with a small metal fitting cuts diagonally across the scene, while a pale sheet of paper blurs in the background. One hand cradles the instrument from the lower right as the extended index finger of a second hand hovers over the upper deck. Throughout, the beads remain broadly in place on their rods, with no obvious sliding toward or away from the beam, so the reckoning configuration changes little. The fingertip drifts only slightly, its motion hard to separate from the slow pan and gentle zoom that shift the left metal border and fitting. Light and shadow move across the rounded surfaces as the angle changes, and the supporting hand makes small adjustments.
